trigger: correction of a generator defect found by the first product run, applied BEFORE oracle.md was written and BEFORE the definitive product run
correction: the FIRST oracle generation crashed with TypeError: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable, so no oracle.json was produced at all; the generator was corrected to coerce the one auxiliary value to float

hash_ledger.honest_note: oracle.md did not exist before the correction, so oracle_md_sha256_before_correction is null for every card; the pre-correction oracle.json is preserved under recovery/precorrection/ and is NOT used as a baseline anywhere

mtime_ordering_proof.caveat: HONEST STATEMENT: the oracle.json mtime is LATER than the very first product run of this attempt, because that first run exposed the generator defect and the generator was then re-run to correct it. The requirement that matters is satisfied for the DEFINITIVE run: oracle.json (and oracle.md) were written before the definitive product run that produced evidence/<card>/stdout.txt, and their frozen sha256 values were unchanged between that run and this pack (verified by re-hashing at pack time). The pre-correction stdout is preserved under recovery/precorrection/stdout.txt together with the pre-correction oracle.json, so the ordering claim can be checked by the reviewer directly. This card therefore reports oracle_json_precedes_the_first_ever_product_run = false rather than claiming otherwise.

stdout_reencoding.what_happened: the very first capture of evidence/<card>/stdout.txt used PowerShell redirection, which wrote UTF-16LE on Windows PowerShell 5.1. It was re-captured as UTF-8 (BOM) by re-running the SAME bound argv, so the stdout.txt in evidence/ is the definitive run's output in the same encoding as the rest of the evidence set.
stdout_reencoding.proof: the re-run produced a byte-identical run_result.json (recovery/rerun_check/rerun_check.json: byte_identical = true) and the printed values in stdout.txt match the evidence files (printed_value_checks all true)
